nodes.claim: The perfect bank serves each person the question that maximizes expected information about them — under the constraint that comparison requires shared ground.
nodes.detail: Pure adaptive selection (ask whatever is most informative next) and pure uniformity (everyone answers everything) are both wrong: the first destroys cohort comparability, the second wastes the answer budget. The perfect axiom is the constrained optimum — a shared spine every person answers (comparability), with the remaining budget allocated adaptively (information). InSight's core/tail split is the practical shadow of exactly this theorem. 2026-08-27: the seed's open problem (the right spine size as a function of population and question count) is refined by que-5 — the size function gains the cross-axiom coupling portfolio as a third argument (entering through dimension coverage), and the spine's composition is set on the joint person-space rather than the bank's own, within que-5's stated boundary; que-6 grounds the spine's linking role in the equating literature. 'Information about them' therefore means information about the joint coordinates, not the bank-internal ones — central's 2026-08-26 question is answered at que-5.

nodes.claim: A question is a measurement instrument with estimable parameters — including which response-process family it obeys — and the perfect bank calibrates those parameters continuously from live answers.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-27; the seed's scout task is answered and the answer resharpened the claim in two places. (i) The instrument frame is canonical: an item carries parameters relative to latent traits — Birnbaum's two-parameter logistic for binary items, Samejima's graded response model for ordinal — and person and item parameters are recovered from response data. One correction to the seed's wording: the workhorse is Bock & Aitkin's MARGINAL maximum likelihood (item parameters estimated by integrating over the ability distribution), not literally joint estimation. (ii) The resharpening: 'difficulty/discrimination' presupposes a DOMINANCE process — endorsement rising monotonically with the trait — which is standard for ability items and contested for opinion and attitude items. Attitude statements often behave as unfolding items: a person disagrees both when the statement is too extreme and when it is too mild, so the response function is single-peaked (Roberts–Donoghue–Laughlin's generalized graded unfolding model; Stark et al. 2006 find ideal-point models fit personality items as well or better; Drasgow et al. 2010 argue Likert-style dominance scoring of such data has been misguided). One term disambiguated by this run's adversarial pass: 'ideal point' names two different model classes — the unfolding sense above (single-peaked response function) and the spatial-voting sense, in which the person carries an ideal point but the item response function is MONOTONE. Clinton–Jackman–Rivers' Bayesian roll-call model is the latter: its quadratic-utility spatial model reduces to a 2PL-equivalent monotone form, so it proves large-scale Bayesian estimation of binary opinion data while sitting on the dominance side, and is cited here as that contrast case, not as unfolding evidence. The perfect bank therefore holds the response-process family per item as an ESTIMABLE property, not an assumption — with the honest limit that the families are not always distinguishable from response data alone (Fu–Tan–Kyllonen 2026: an unfolding model can reproduce a dominance model's curves given an informative prior at, or fixing of, an extreme item location). (iii) 'Calibrates continuously' is a real literature, not a metaphor: online item calibration in operational adaptive testing (van der Linden & Ren's optimal Bayesian calibration design; Ren–van der Linden–Diao's continuous online calibration), with Stocking 1988 naming the standing failure mode — scale drift when live calibration optimizes against current estimates. (iv) InSight connection kept from the seed: the nightly fit's published loading vectors are item parameters in all but name; selection (que-1/que-5) should run on measured item profiles rather than topic labels — the first REQUESTS row asks for exactly that exposure. Verification note: this container's egress policy blocks publisher full-text; every source was corroborated at search-index/metadata level against the publisher's own indexed record plus at least one independent record (the body lane's 2026-08-27 precedent), and the full set was independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass. nodes.claim: Question production is generation-plus-calibration under a warmth constraint: generated items inherit family-level parameter distributions from their authoring structure, never known parameters; the feature-to-parameter map is modelable (LLTM through explanatory IRT) but no blind benchmark has shown it forecasting well enough to replace calibration, so the map is calibration's prior and hypothesis-generator, never its substitute; and the guardrail's home-domain evidence establishes what engagement-optimized ranking selects — out-group animosity, diverging from users' stated preference — not that it changes readers; the closed loop as one system, and its two transfers (platform→bank, ability→opinion), are this lane's marked inferences.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-09-01; the grounding path queued 2026-08-27 was scouted, and the first draft's claim and detail were rebuilt by this run's adversarial pass (7 blocking + 10 should-fix + 6 lesser defects, all applied pre-land) — the claim now asserts only what the limbs' sources establish, with the closed loop as one system, and its two transfers, held here as this lane's marked inferences: no source measures a full authored→measured→re-authored bank across generations. (i) Generation. Generated items never come with KNOWN parameters, only with family-level parameter DISTRIBUTIONS — a correction the sources themselves insist on. Embretson 1999 states the problem class (on-line generation vs the axiom of measuring people from items of known properties) and the repairing model class — calibrate the generating principles, not the specific items. Glas & van der Linden's item-cloning CAT makes within-family item parameters random draws from family hyperparameters; its headline warning is this node's correction (ignoring within-family variability biases ability estimates). Geerlings–Glas–van der Linden give the published form of family parameters tied to authoring rules: a hierarchical IRT model for items generated by combinations of design rules, items within a family ASSUMED to differ only in surface features — a modelling assumption, not a finding — estimated in a Bayesian framework and applied to a non-verbal intelligence test. Gierl & Haladyna stands in the source list as the field's reference volume, with no specific content claim hung on it. The neural half generates but does not predict: von Davier's LSTM emits well-formed personality-questionnaire items without construct targeting; Attali et al. ran a large-scale PILOT — their own word, contrasted in the paper itself with 'the operational DET' — of a transformer generation pipeline in the Duolingo English Test practice test, human review retaining 58% of generated passages and live responses analyzed psychometrically: feasibility under human review, the generate→measure half of the loop, not measure→predict and not operational deployment. (ii) Prediction. The feature→parameter map is half a century old as a model: Fischer's linear logistic test model decomposes Rasch difficulty into weights on authoring operations, the weights estimated from response data — the documented ancestor of 'measured performance teaches the next question's shape' — and De Boeck & Wilson's explanatory frame generalizes item properties to covariates, LLTM's hard linear constraint relaxed by random-item models (De Boeck 2008 — the reason limb (i)'s family models exist). As a blind forecast the record is thin and stays unverdicted: on the one shared blind benchmark of text-based prediction for human-authored items — BEA 2024, 667 retired USMLE MCQs — the best system's test-split RMSE beat a predict-the-mean baseline only marginally (≈0.29 vs ≈0.31; response time proved easier to predict, on its own non-comparable scale); successor results are not scale-comparable across datasets (fine-tuned LMs later beat the BEA winner on the same data, Li et al. 2025; the surveys' round-ups carry far lower best-case figures on easier in-domain datasets) — which is the surveys' own point (Benedetto et al.; AlKhuzaey et al.): no accuracy verdict is licensed in either direction; and no comparable blind benchmark exists for rule-generated families, where limb (i)'s models predict at family level by construction. What stands: no blind benchmark has shown the map forecasting well enough to replace calibration, so the loop closes through live calibration (que-2, a depends edge), the learned map its prior and hypothesis-generator — 'teaches the next question's shape' means informative priors and authoring bets, not pre-known parameters. And a second transfer, marked like the platform one: every prediction source here is ability/cognitive, where difficulty is defined against a correct answer; the one opinion-shaped source (von Davier) is precisely the one that generates without predicting. For que-2's opinion-shaped bank the analogue of difficulty is item location/thresholds (or ideal-point location under unfolding), and no cited source estimates a feature→location map for opinion items — that map's existence for THIS bank is hypothesis, not import. (iii) The guardrail — warmth as a constraint standing outside que-8's bits currency (in the product's own rule, warmth over evenness) — now argued from home-domain evidence, its transfer marked. What engagement optimization SELECTS is established: in a preregistered algorithmic audit manipulating the objective (Milli et al.), engagement-based ranking amplified content expressing partisanship and out-group animosity relative to a reverse-chronological baseline, amplified content users say makes them feel worse about their political out-group, and diverged from users' stated preferences. The correlational background points the same way (Brady et al. 2017 — observational, diffusion up roughly 20% per additional moral-emotional word, bounded within ideological networks; Rathje et al. — n≈2.7M posts, out-group language the strongest sharing predictor, well ahead of moral-emotional language), and Brady et al. 2021 supplies the loop mechanism at the person level: positive social feedback on outrage expression raises the probability of subsequent outrage expression, consistent with reinforcement learning — measured reward reshaping the next utterance's shape, this node's loop pointed at the failure mode. What is NOT established, held openly per que-4's controversy precedent: that the selection changes readers — the domain's largest randomized experiment (Guess et al. 2023: engagement-ranked feeds swapped for reverse-chronological for three months in a US election campaign) changed exposure substantially, roughly halving hateful/intolerant content, yet moved no measured polarization outcome. The guardrail needs only the selection half: a bank whose objective converges on outrage-shaped items is a worse INSTRUMENT for every other axiom's purposes whatever it does to its readers — but 'a bank optimized for maximal disagreement converges on outrage' remains this lane's TRANSFER of platform evidence to item banks, an analogy stated as one. The guardrail also REFINES que-1 rather than supporting it: for opinion items the maximum-expected-information item is approximately the maximally splitting one, so an unconstrained que-1 optimizer walks toward exactly this failure mode — the que-1 edge is retyped accordingly, and a supports edge to que-8 records that que-8's second outside-the-currency constraint is this limb. (iv) InSight connection kept and sharpened: the scorecard's evenness and vintage comparisons are the loop's shadow; the first REQUESTS row (item-information profiles) is its parameter side; this run's REQUESTS row asks for the feature side — most shape features are already committed on the bank (type, options, tone, cat, D187's rates), so what is missing is the derived features and their publication as one joinable table. nodes.claim: Portability across culture and language is established per question and cohort, never assumed — and comparison is graded to the level of invariance actually established, labeled with its basis.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-27, and the claim WEAKENED into its defensible form on the scout's evidence: the seed said 'refuses cross-cohort comparison where invariance fails', but the literature says the refusal must be graded, because exact invariance rarely holds across many groups and methods exist precisely to define what comparison remains legal beneath it. Grounding: the invariance taxonomy — configural through strict factorial — and why comparability precedes comparison (Meredith 1993; Davidov et al. 2014 is the umbrella review); partial invariance as the original definition of legal comparison under failure (Byrne–Shavelson–Muthén 1989); alignment and Bayesian approximate invariance as many-group methods that permit mean/variance comparison WITHOUT exact invariance (Asparouhov & Muthén 2014; van de Schoot et al. 2013); the construct/method/item-bias taxonomy separating translation and cultural context as distinct threat classes (van de Vijver & Tanzer 2004); and the empirical anchor that translation itself moves item functioning — differential item functioning grows with linguistic and cultural distance across TIMSS's 57 countries and 43 languages, with language-version differences more influential than country differences (Gökçe et al. 2021). Held honestly, the live controversy: Welzel et al. argue in print that detected non-invariance is often artifactual (closed-ended scale arithmetic under sample-mean disparity) and that invariance testing blocks substantively valid comparisons; Meuleman et al. answer in the same journal that the statistical argument is wrong; Funder & Gardiner argue conventional invariance benchmarks are strict enough to effectively prohibit cross-cultural research and urge external validity as the better criterion. The perfect axiom's rule is therefore not 'invariance or silence' but InSight's honesty grammar generalized: establish the level of comparability per question and cohort by a NAMED method (exact, partial, approximate, alignment), license only the comparisons that level supports, state the basis with the reading — and refuse outright only where even graded comparability cannot be established. Verification note: publisher full-text egress-blocked from this container; all sources corroborated at search-index/metadata level, each against at least two independent records, and independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass.

nodes.claim: The combination bends the spine twice — composition toward identifying the joint person-space, size through the coupling portfolio's dimension-coverage floor; within-bank information alone selects the right spine only in the degenerate case where the joint space is a nonsingular reparameterization of the bank's own and no cross-instrument map remains to be estimated.
nodes.detail: Answers central's 2026-08-26 question directly: no, the optimal spine is not chosen for within-bank information alone — with the claim's boundary stated first, because the strongest objection comes from que-6's own formalism: D-optimality is invariant under nonsingular reparameterization, so if the joint coordinates were merely a nonsingular relabeling of what the bank already measures, and every cross-instrument map were already known, the within-bank D-optimal spine WOULD be the joint one. The bend is real exactly where InSight's case breaks those conditions: other axioms measure dimensions the bank reaches weakly or not at all, and the cross-instrument maps are themselves still under estimation. Three arguments. (1) Intersection mass: adaptive tails fragment item-level answered populations by design, so the spine is the only part of the bank whose per-item n grows like the whole population; a questions×other-axiom coupling's n is the intersection of the axioms' populations (pat-4), and at item level the question-side membership of that intersection is essentially the spine — comparability inside the bank (que-1's original framing) is only half the spine's job. The channel stated precisely, per the adversarial pass: once an item is in the spine everyone answers it, so ADDING spine items does not raise any coupling's n. Intersection mass is delivered by spine membership; size enters at (3) through coverage, not through n. (2) Composition: the estimand decides the optimum, and the joint criterion splits the budget between two item roles. LINKING items content-overlap what another axiom measures and identify the cross-instrument map onto the shared space — a same-construct bridging estimand: coupling geometry between DISTINCT constructs needs only jointly measured people, which spine membership already supplies, but identifying how the bank's scale maps onto another instrument's requires items touching that instrument's construct. COMPLEMENTARY items add joint information conditional on what the other axioms already pin — an item duplicating what sensors measure well adds little; an item on a dimension no other axiom reaches adds much. The split is a continuum (the angle between an item's information direction and the already-measured subspace), not a partition. How the optimal split moves over the program's life is an explicit PREDICTION, not a derivation: pinning the maps should release linking budget toward complementarity, but each newly priced coupling or newly added axiom renews linking demand — which pressure dominates is an empirical question, and the split's trajectory would itself be a measurable signal of the combination's maturity. (3) Size: the portfolio floors spine size through dimension coverage. Each priced coupling names question-side dimensions that must be measured to a target reliability for everyone in the intersection ('target reliability' is this node's construct, layered on pat-4's budget-and-marginal-value frame — pat-4 does not itself assign per-coupling precision targets); reliability per dimension requires a minimum item count, and the dimensions needing coverage multiply with axioms and priced pairs. So que-1's open problem gains an argument: spine size is f(population, bank size, coupling portfolio), the portfolio entering through which dimensions must be covered and how well. Two inherited fragilities, named: cen-1 is argued and flags its own fork (if audit-layer faithfulness cannot be measured, the published joint coordinate system degrades from specification to aspiration) — this node's composition argument inherits that fork. And an open tension with que-6 stood deliberately at landing: que-6's anchor logic wants the spine to span what the BANK measures, this node wants composition set on the JOINT space; under a fixed answer budget those compete for the same slots. 2026-08-29: that tension is now PRICED at que-8 (scaffolding at que-7) — one constrained optimization above a graded validity floor — and que-8 prices angles on this node's continuum rather than re-partitioning it; the linking↔complementarity drift prediction gains its observable there (the sign and movement of que-8's composite rate). Status held at argued deliberately: the equating and optimal-design scaffolding is cited at que-6, but the cross-axiom bending itself is this lane's own argument — no external source claims it, and §4 says the status stays down.

nodes.claim: The shared spine plays the anchor set's linking role from equating theory — and the mini-version prescription is partly relaxable: with content coverage and mean difficulty held, a narrower difficulty spread equates about as well.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27 as the grounded scaffolding under que-5; claim narrowed by the adversarial pass before landing to exactly what the cited evidence tested. The spine's linking role is the same structure as the common-item nonequivalent-groups design — classical two-form NEAT is the special case; InSight's spine-plus-adaptive-tail is item-pool linking as in CAT calibration — where the common items are what make measurements from people who otherwise answered different item sets comparable. The field's standard prescription, that the anchor be a miniature of the full instrument in content and statistical specifications, is documented at first hand in Sinharay & Holland's own abstract (their study 'questioned conventional wisdom that an anchor test should be a statistical miniature version of the tests being equated'); Kolen & Brennan stands in the source list as the standard text of the field, with no specific page-level content claim hung on it — it was not readable at first hand from this container. What Sinharay & Holland actually tested and found: holding content coverage representative and mean item difficulty equal, anchors with a NARROWER spread of item difficulty equated about as well as mini-version anchors — so the spread half of statistical mimicry is relaxable, and their result licenses nothing about relaxing content coverage or mean difficulty; this node deliberately claims nothing beyond it. For InSight: the spine should cover the content of what needs linking — per que-5, that is bent toward the joint space. The que-5↔que-6 budget tension both nodes named at landing (span the bank vs identify the joint space under one fixed budget) is priced 2026-08-29 at que-8: content coverage enters there as a graded validity constraint (que-4's rungs), not a bits-priced term — consistent with this node's bound that Sinharay & Holland licensed nothing about relaxing coverage, while their spread result is reread there, carefully, as a measured near-zero price on the one dimension they did test. The selection formalism que-1 and que-5 lean on is likewise standard: item choice as maximization of information about the estimand (van der Linden 1998 for the Bayesian criterion; van der Linden 2005 for test assembly as constrained optimization), and Berger–King–Wong for the D-optimality frame together with its standard robustification — information-optimal designs are locally optimal, i.e. optimal against current parameter estimates (que-2's calibration-drift warning in design form), and minimax design is the paper's remedy for exactly that. nodes.claim: With a log-score utility, expected information is a special case of expected utility, and sequential experimental design prices an entire experiment sequence in that single unit over a horizon — myopic design the suboptimal special case that drops the future term — so deferred information carries a present shadow value in the same unit as immediate information.
nodes.detail: The scaffolding under que-8, each limb grounded and each limb's limit stated; the claim is deliberately narrowed to what the cited machinery establishes, with this lane's further inference held below, marked as inference. (i) Lindley 1956 defines the information provided by an experiment as expected reduction in Shannon entropy over the parameter, explicitly for design; Bernardo 1979 proves that maximizing expected information is A SPECIAL CASE OF expected-utility maximization — for an appropriate decision space (reporting a probability distribution) and a smoothness/locality constraint on the utility, under the paper's own premise that the scientist lacks a clear utility of results: a licence to use bits AS a utility where no real utility is available, not a demonstration that real utilities reduce to bits. The propriety parenthetical, qualified per this run's adversarial pass: the log score is strictly proper and the unique smooth local proper score on sample spaces with MORE THAN TWO outcomes (Dawid–Musio's characterization holds for #X>2) — a qualification that bites here, since binary items are the bank's common case. And cen-2's yardstick is the same score applied to the one-step predictive distribution rather than to a report about the parameter: the two coincide as design criteria only under well-specification, and cen-2's cross-axiom conditional form is not Lindley–Bernardo expected information gain — the identification is a choice of instantiation this program makes, not a corollary. (ii) Howard 1966's value of information prices resolving uncertainty whose payoff accrues through a subsequent decision, as a present expected value in the decision currency — commensuration of information with utility WITHIN one decision problem; it supplies no temporal structure (no horizon, no discounting, no stream), and its premise — a known economic value structure — is the opposite of Bernardo's, so limbs (i) and (ii) bridge information and utility from opposite ends under mutually exclusive premises; neither alone carries the claim. (iii) The limb that does carry it: Chaloner & Verdinelli 1995 place information-based design in the decision-theoretic frame where a design's value is the expected utility of everything that follows it; Huan–Jagalur–Marzouk 2024 survey the modern formulation including sequential optimal experimental design in dynamic-programming form, where non-myopic policies coordinate all experiments to be performed and greedy (myopic) design is the suboptimal special case that drops the future term — myopic suboptimality IS the statement that later bits carry present shadow value in the same unit. (iv) Gittins 1979 is cited as a DISANALOGY that locates the difficulty, not as support for a one-index reduction: index optimality needs Markovian, mutually independent arms that are frozen while not selected, one pull at a time, and a common geometric discount over an infinite horizon. Spine items violate independence (they interact through the joint model) and, more damagingly, restedness — item and map parameters drift whether or not an item is selected (que-2's Stocking warning), which makes the spine a restless bandit, where Whittle-index policies are only approximately optimal and indexability itself can fail. (v) Dawid 1984's prequential framework makes the unit operational — assess a forecasting system on its sequential one-step-ahead forecasts of the actually-arriving stream, with the prequential principle proper constraining any such assessment to depend only on the forecasts issued and the outcomes observed — the score family cen-2 adopted and D325's quality block ships the answer-only floor of. This lane's inference from the limbs, marked as inference and no source's claim: inside one fixed decision problem, a bits-now vs bits-later standoff is a weighting-and-risk question within a single optimization rather than an incommensurability — que-8 applies this and carries the argument. Honest limits: commensuration is operative only once a horizon and weighting are CHOSEN — a governance input, not an estimate (que-8 takes this up); log-loss is comparable only on a common observable sequence, and que-8's trade compares bits on today's answer stream against bits on a future joint stream over a growing axiom set — no common measure space at the horizon, so 'one currency' there is a modelling assumption, not a theorem; under misspecification the prequential loss stays well-defined and measurable while the design-optimality guarantees do not — the yardstick survives where the theorems lapse; and a discounted SUM of per-step log scores is not the log score of any joint predictive distribution, so the aggregate objective forfeits the propriety/uniqueness argument, geometric discounting being equivalent to assuming a geometric program-termination hazard. nodes.claim: The que-5↔que-6 tension resolves as one constrained optimization in cen-2's currency, not a two-currency standoff: a graded comparability floor — a validity constraint imported from outside the currency, rung-indexed per que-4, never priced in bits — with every slot above it valued in expected program-horizon prequential bits, a linking item's deferred bits carrying a locally-valid weight of per-paired-person prediction rate × pairing arrival × map survival, whose exponential reduced form is central's scalar discount rate — sign not guaranteed.
nodes.detail: Answers central's 2026-08-28 question directly: yes, one currency (scaffolding at que-7) — but the correct single statement is a CONSTRAINED optimization, and the constraint is where the two-currency intuition came from. The first draft's floor argument and weight decomposition were reconstructed by this run's adversarial pass; what stands is the amended form. (1) The floor, as validity rather than scoreability: comparability is NOT a precondition of scoring — held-out predictive surprisal is computable with no equating at all, which is why D325's answer-only block ships today while que-4's invariance levels are largely unestablished. It is a precondition of the objective's MEANING: a bits-optimal bank whose coordinates denote different constructs in different cohorts optimizes a well-defined number over an estimand nobody wants. The floor is therefore a validity constraint imported from outside the currency — and it is GRADED, not a cliff: que-4 supplies rungs (configural, partial, approximate, alignment), each licensing a comparison class, so the constraint is a required rung per comparison class, and which rung each class must clear is a governance input alongside the horizon — the optimization is horizon-indexed AND rung-indexed. Sinharay & Holland belong on the pricing side of this line, read carefully: they MEASURED the cost of relaxing one dimension of anchor mimicry (difficulty spread) and found it near zero — a flat region of a trade-off curve — and tested nothing about content coverage, so their result neither prices coverage nor exempts it (que-6's own bound). The felt incommensurability was the shadow of constraint-plus-objective structure: the currencies commensurate above the floor, and the floor was never a currency. That answers central's counterargument invitation — with the boundary that que-3's warmth guardrail is a second constraint standing outside the currency; this node's scope is spine composition under both. (2) The roles and the weight. Three roles on que-5's continuum, not a partition: an item sits at two angles — to the bank's own content (que-6's anchor coverage) and to the already-measured other-axiom subspace (que-5's complementarity) — with linking items defined by content-overlapping another axiom's construct; the priced trade is over a simplex of angles, and 'spanning' and 'complementary' are NOT the same role. All roles are integrals of the same instantaneous quantity — expected one-step-ahead surprisal reduction on the joint stream — over the program horizon; they differ in payoff shape, not unit. An anchor or complementary item pays front-loaded, near-certain bits on the answer stream, depreciating CONTINUOUSLY with item-parameter drift (que-2's Stocking warning) — depreciation is a falling bits-per-prediction curve, never a 0/1 gate. A linking item's deferred bits carry a weight of per-paired-person cross-axiom prediction rate × pairing-arrival probability × map-estimate survival, with three honesty clauses: the first factor is defined PER PAIRED PERSON precisely so pairing is not counted twice (raw prediction volume already contains the paired population); the factors multiply as an approximation valid only under independence, which shared causes plausibly violate (program traffic drives pairing, refit cadence and prediction volume together); and the weight is a linearisation — marginal linking value falls along the map learning curve, so the true object is a set function, plausibly non-submodular, and a per-item weight is valid only locally around the current portfolio. Reconciliation with cen-2, a declared dependency: cen-2's rule — thin pairing widens error bars on value, does not zero it — is about an axiom's definitional value on the common population; this weight prices the realisation TIMING of a spine slot's deferred bits: arrival moves the expected date and volume of the bits, never the claim's truth. Myopic selection systematically UNDERBUYS linking items rather than never buying them: their one-step term is positive but small — some answer-stream information, plus cross-axiom bits for the existing intersection que-5's membership argument guarantees — while their large term is the growth of the intersection they will later serve; the non-myopic formulation (que-7) is what makes that deferred term visible, and it also prices the option value of DEFERRING — buying linking items later, once maps are better identified and pairing thicker, can dominate buying now. Central's scalar discount rate is the reduced form under one further collapse: if each factor is exponential with constant rate, the composite is a single exponential — and the sign is not guaranteed, since rate and arrival grow while survival decays; a negative composite means future bits worth MORE than present ones. Which sign holds is an empirical question the four curves answer — so central's discount framing is confirmed conditionally, not absolutely. (3) What data locates the optimum — four measurable curves: (i) the map learning curve — held-out cross-axiom surprisal against linking investment at fixed pairing; needs cross-axiom prequential logging, which does not yet exist — the single-stream identity is a specification and this curve is its test, not an illustration (cen-2 names the score family; D325 ships the answer-only floor); (ii) within-bank marginal item information — the lane's first REQUESTS row; (iii) depreciation, split by branch: within-bank loading drift (this run's REQUESTS row — the anchor/complementary branch's depreciation, measurable from the nightly fit today, requiring a named alignment method and a refit-noise null or the number is uninterpretable) and cross-instrument map drift (the linking branch's survival factor — measurable only once maps are estimated at all); (iv) pairing arrival — paired-population growth per pair, pat-4's bookkeeping. (4) Honest residues, kept outside the arithmetic: horizon, weighting and required rungs are governance inputs — no data settles them; they index the optimization. The horizon integral is over a fixed joint stream, and each newly instrumented axiom redefines the stream, so the objective is re-based rather than continued (que-7's measure-space limit, inherited). Status held at argued deliberately: the machinery is cited at que-7, but the validity-floor argument, the two-angle role geometry and the weight decomposition are this lane's own construction — no external source states them for this problem, and §4 keeps the status down.
